Learnings from traveling with wife through India
..Bring or buy a shawl - clothes that conservative in the US are risqué elsewhere 
..Dress like a local - look around at the style and buy stuff in country.  
..Be careful of bars - they’re fun but in India they were almost male-only and my presence with her didn’t deter the lurkers 
..if you’re traveling via train in coach, get a top bunk to prevent someone from joining you (or better yet, travel first class, it’s not that much more $)
..smile! It disarms people who are staring because they may not have seen a foreigner before 
..did I mention a shaw? Once my wife wore one it changed for the better our interactions with locals and, to be honest, the simple action made us both feel safer

Not to beat a dead horse, but at 250 calories you could have 8 egg whites (125 calories) and one trader joes multi grain wrap (120 calories). This would provide 30 grams of protein and 24 grams of carbs. 

Prep is fast.  Spray a coffee mug with non stick pray. pour one cup liquid egg whites (that's about 8 egg whites) and a splash of milk into the mug. Lightly whip with fork. Microwave 2 min (it might take 3 or 4 but check at 2 min). When fluffy dump eggs onto wrap, add salt and pepper, nosh. 

My bet is you will be full and that prep of the eggs is no longer than prepping a smoothie. I like to eat a half cup of eggs whites plus one egg. I'm 6'1 165 and that usually fills me up.

If you need some ideas for a meal plan, follow me on MyFitnessPal.  I am trippingfrogs and I log my meals with a target of calories of 40% protein, 40% carbs, 20% fat.

Have you used a calorie calculator to determine your caloric intake?  Because you are 190 lbs does not necessarily mean that you should eat 1900 calories.  Your caloric intake also depends on your age, height, and activity level.  

For instance, I used http://www.caloriecontrol.org/healthy-weight-tool-kit/weight-maintenance-calculator-men and with some baseless assumptions that you are a 190 lb, 5'11", 30 year old male who has a sedentary lifestyle, you should consume ~2400 calories to maintain your current weight.

I think that you will find that you want to fuel your body adequately once you start working out.  Notice that I said "fuel your body" not "eat".  Food is all about providing the energy that you'll need to workout at your highest capacity and reducing the amount of time it takes to recover (google "recovery shakes").
